text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The biggest opposition parties IMRO-DPMNY and the Democratic Party on Monday signed an agreement on cooperation during local elections. Their joint candidate for Skopje mayor is Democratic party Secretary General Risto Penov.
- Macedonian Parliament speaker Tito Petkovski obtained support for Macedonia's admission to the CEFTA during his visit to Poland.
- Macedonian and Yugoslav defence ministers Blagoje Handziski and Pavle Bulatovic agreed the two countries' border should be defined as soon as possible.

- Stojan Andov, the leader of the opposition Liberal Party told Greek paper Elefterotipija that "there is a serious disagreement between Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov and the government over foreign policy". The Liberal Party became an opposition party after ruling Alliance for Macedonia broke up.
- Greece interested in investing in Macedonia in the field of transport and energy.
- Macedonian government authorises imports of 40,000 tonnes of corn and 20,000 tonnes of barley for cattle raising.
- Austrian company ACTY started the construction of a tunnel on the railroad towards Bulgaria. Macedonian railways obtained 650,000 German marks for regulating the debt to the Austrian company.
- Croatian media expresses reservations over the customs- free regime between Yugoslavia and Macedonia which entered into effect on Monday.
